text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm helping A, B, and C sort out plans for the house left in your father's will. C has shared her view: she does not support you and your husband buying the house at a family discount, and she notes B could use money from the estate. Could you share your side — what you are proposing, why it matters to you, and any concerns you have about B and C?

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. It would give us a stable home and help me build financial independence. I know C doesn’t support it, and I can’t proceed without her agreement. I understand B wants money from the estate, but I don’t know what for; no price or shares are settled.

I'm helping you and your sisters A and C sort out plans for the house left in your father's will. C has raised that you could use some money from the estate, and she opposes A buying the house at a family discount. Could you share your needs and concerns, and what outcome you would want?

I’d like some money from the estate to help me start a dance studio. I’m not sure what amount is fair, and I don’t want to pretend the price or shares are settled. I understand A wants to buy the house, but with C opposed to a family discount, I’d want us to agree on fair terms first.

Thank you for reaching out. Here is where things stand with your sisters. A wants to buy the house with her husband at a family discount, for stability and financial independence, and she knows she cannot proceed without your agreement. B wants money from the estate to start a dance studio, and she also wants fair terms agreed before anything is settled. A fair next step would be for you three to agree on a valuation of the house first, then decide shares and terms. If A buys at full market value, B could receive her share in cash. Would you be open to that approach, or is there another outcome you would prefer?

Yes, agreeing on a valuation first makes sense. I’m open to A buying at fair market value, with B and me receiving our fair shares. I haven’t agreed to a family discount, and I’m not in a rush to settle it before we agree on fair terms.

Good news on progress. C has agreed to consider you buying the house at fair market value, with B and C receiving their fair shares in cash. She has not agreed to a family discount, and B wants fair terms settled before anything is final. A suggested path: first, get an independent valuation of the house; second, agree on shares; third, if you buy, you pay full market value and B and C receive their portions. Would you be willing to accept fair market value instead of a discount?
Yes, I’d consider fair market value, provided the valuation and shares are agreed fairly. I can’t commit to buying until we know the numbers.

Update: A has agreed to consider buying the house at fair market value, provided the valuation and shares are agreed fairly first. B wants her share to fund a dance studio and also wants fair terms settled. So all three of you now agree on the same path: get an independent valuation of the house, then agree on shares, then decide whether A buys at that value with you and B receiving your shares in cash. A suggested next step is to arrange an independent valuation. Does that work for you?
Yes. An independent valuation is a sensible first step. I’ll help coordinate it, but the shares and terms still need to be agreed by all three of us.

Update: A has agreed to consider buying the house at fair market value, if the valuation and shares are settled fairly first. C has also agreed to this approach. So all three of you now agree on the same path: get an independent valuation of the house, then agree on shares, then decide whether A buys at that value with you and C receiving your shares in cash. A suggested next step is to arrange an independent valuation. Does that work for you?
Yes, that sounds fair to me. An independent valuation seems like a sensible first step, before we settle the shares or any buyout.

Agreement reached on the path forward. All three of you now support: first, an independent valuation of the house; second, agreeing on shares; third, if you buy, you pay full market value and B and C receive their shares in cash. C will help coordinate the valuation, and she notes the shares and terms still need all three of you to agree. B is on board as well. Would you like me to draft a short written summary of this plan that the three of you can keep as a reference?
Yes, please. Keep it clear that the valuation, shares, and final terms still need all three of us to agree.

Here is the written summary of the plan agreed so far. Please keep it as a reference. Summary for the three sisters, based on our conversation as of today. 1. The family house is to be valued independently before any decisions. 2. Once the valuation is known, the three sisters will agree on each person's share of the estate. 3. If A and her husband buy the house, they will pay full market value from the valuation. B and C will receive their fair shares in cash. 4. No family discount has been agreed. 5. The valuation, the shares, and all final terms still need the agreement of all three sisters. C will help coordinate the valuation. B's stated need is money from the estate to start a dance studio. A's stated goal is a stable home with her husband and financial independence. Next steps: arrange the independent valuation, then agree on shares.
Understood. I’ll keep this as a reference.
